description:
Close-out of review finding C3: after #1176 (requested_config_hash) and the
applied-ledger PR land, the explorer pipeline should read the bundle's
hashes rather than computing its own 8-char mode hash
(_project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/transformer.py _tuning_hash). Legacy
bundles without the new fields keep the current honest fallback (mode-only
or none). Receipt display shows which hash kind it is (requested vs applied)
instead of an ambiguous "hash xxxx" suffix; a mode-only fallback displays as
mode, not as a pseudo-fingerprint (closes the receipt cosmetic nit from
#1170's review).

deferrals.reason: node_modules not installed locally -> npm test/build cannot run in this session; adding blind TS tests risks CI red with no capacity to fix under a session limit. Existing TS receipt tests exercise the new hashRow code path with null values + CI verifies the build. Follow-up: add non-null-path assertions.
deferrals.summary: TS unit tests for the non-null requested/applied hash path in RunReceipt + ComparabilityReceipt mode-only fallback

deferrals.reason: w4, deferred from #1182. Needs new plumbing (facet not flowing cleanly); out of the w1-w3 hash-ingest core. Assess+implement as a follow-up.
deferrals.summary: Surface physical_rendering_id secondary facet in the explorer UI (chip/filter)

preserves.behavior: Legacy bundle ingest (no new fields) keeps current behavior
tuning_hash column remains display-only (never a join/dedup key)

verifications.expected: All passing; new-generation bundle rows carry both hashes
